Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 30 ApiError.category union = network, timeout, authentication, authorization, validation, business, conflict, rate_limit, server, contract, cancelled, unknown; includes fieldErrors. Doc 34 union = network, timeout, authentication, authorization, validation, not_found, conflict, rate_limit, server, contract, business, unknown; no fieldErrors, adds status and code. Doc 30 §12.1 also lists Not Found Error that its own union does not model.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Two non-identical TypeScript shapes for the same type name; form field errors have no representation in doc 34.
Notes: Both documents state the model is illustrative and not the final contract (30 §12.2 'این مدل نمونه است', 34 §8.2 'صرفاً نمونه طراحی است'). No unconditional requirement is violated, which is why severity drops from P0 to P1.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Three complete security standards govern the same domain. Requirement text is compatible: all three leave cookie-vs-token open and all three recommend HttpOnly/SameSite as candidates. The defect is identifier collision, not contradictory requirements.
Technical or Documentation Impact: No requirement contradiction found. Traceability is ambiguous because SEC-Dxx resolves differently per document.
Notes: No conflicting MUST-level statement was found between 22, 24 and 31. Reclassified from 'conflict' to scope overlap plus identifier collision. Severity P0 to P1.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Both documents set WCAG 2.2 Level AA, both give 4.5:1 normal and 3:1 large/UI contrast, both define acceptance criteria and both keep the target as proposed. Targets are identical; the criteria sets and decision registers are parallel.
Technical or Documentation Impact: A component can pass one acceptance table and fail the other; release gate QG-09 has no designated source.
Notes: Confirmed as duplication, not contradiction. Prior register already classified it organizational.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 06 classifies components into seven domain categories (Foundations, Form, Navigation, Feedback, Data, Business, Scientific). Doc 14 classifies into four structural levels with explicit ID tables. Both also define a component contract (06 §12, 14 §4).
Technical or Documentation Impact: Component registry structure and package boundaries cannot be fixed until one taxonomy governs.
Notes: Genuine specification conflict because two incompatible classification schemes are normative. No product breaks immediately, hence P2.

Technical or Documentation Impact: Values agree at 768, 1024, 1280, 1536 but 360 and 480 exist only in doc 20 and 640 exists only in doc 06.
Notes: Both are explicitly provisional (06 §9.3 'مقادیر پیشنهادی برای بررسی', 20 §4 'نقطه شروع پیشنهادی هستند و نهایی نیستند'). Downgraded to P3 because no requirement is final.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 14 §4 uses React.ReactNode in a code sample. Doc 15 §26 says 'in a React architecture ... is recommended'. Doc 22 §20 says 'in React applications Error Boundary can ...'. Doc 23 §8 is titled REACT PERFORMANCE STANDARDS but its body says 'if React is used'. Doc 27 §6.1 lists React Rendering Errors as a mandatory error category. Doc 29 §14.1 lists 'compatibility with React' as a selection criterion and §14.2 gives React-only examples.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Five of six statements are conditional or illustrative. Two are assertive: 27 §6.1 (error category) and 29 §14.1 (selection criterion). No document states a contradictory framework requirement.
Notes: Not a cross-document conflict: no second party asserts a different framework. The real finding is a missing framework decision, confirmed separately as decision B01. Prior register mislabelled it as a conflict.

Technical or Documentation Impact: Version comparison and maturity inference break in any documentation pipeline.
Notes: All documents remain unapproved under every scheme; this is presentation consistency only.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Thirty-four documents are Persian-primary with mixed English headings; documents 36 and 37 are English-only. No document declares an authoring-language policy.
Technical or Documentation Impact: The same concepts are worded in two languages without a shared normative glossary.
Notes: Not a requirement conflict; a governance and terminology issue.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 14 says financial values 'باید' (must) be handled with Decimal. Doc 36 says the frontend 'SHOULD' preserve decimal input as a string. Doc 34 §15.2 says Decimal modelling is 'الزامی پیشنهادی' (recommended-mandatory). Doc 31 §14 prohibits Decimal-to-float conversion.
Technical or Documentation Impact: The same rule carries three different obligation levels, so a reviewer cannot decide whether float conversion is a defect or an accepted deviation.
Notes: Real normative inconsistency. Direction is consistent across all documents; only strength differs.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 15 separates UI state from server state; doc 29 classifies local, shared UI, server, URL, form, auth, application and domain state. The models are compatible. Cache policy appears as D-015-04 and as STATE-D06/D07; offline as D-015-06 and STATE-D10/D11.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Same decisions recorded twice under two identifier families; approval workflow will duplicate.
Notes: Content consistent; only ownership duplicated.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Two full standards cover API integration, contracts and error handling. Decision registers are disjoint but describe the same choices: API-D05 vs D-034-03 (response envelope), API-D06 vs D-034-04 (error format), API-D09 vs D-034-08 (retry and timeout), API-D10 vs D-034-09 (idempotency).
Technical or Documentation Impact: No document can be cited as the API baseline; 44 decisions stand where about 20 are needed.
Notes: Duplicate scope rather than contradictory requirements. P0 to P1 because no requirement is violated, only authority is unclear.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Logotype architecture is cited as an existing standard and does not exist.
Technical or Documentation Impact: No rule for logo construction, clear space, minimum size, lockups or three-brand co-branding.
Notes: P0 within brand scope; P1 for the current sequence. Resolution options: locate outside directory, author, or formally fold into 05 §8 and 09 §4.

Actual Statement or Requirement: No document records an application framework decision; six documents presuppose React in varying degrees.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Every technical provision has an unrecorded precondition.
Notes: Moved to decision register as B01. Not a documentation coverage gap; a missing decision.

Actual Statement or Requirement: No dedicated authentication and authorization standard exists; the topic is distributed across three security standards with colliding identifiers.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Authentication, session, MFA, role model and tenant isolation have no single owner document.
Notes: Priority lowered because all three documents are internally consistent on the requirements themselves.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Two complete API standards with disjoint decision registers covering the same choices.
Technical or Documentation Impact: No API baseline can be cited; decisions duplicate.
Notes: Same finding as CONF-013.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 20 §24 names supported families: Chromium-based, Firefox, Safari, Mobile Safari, Android browsers, and states target versions must be chosen by real user share, security requirements and maintainability. Doc 32 §26.4 lists NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack, browser zoom and high-contrast modes.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Families and ATs are named; minimum versions and the ratified support matrix are absent.
Notes: Prior report claimed 'not covered'. Incorrect: families and assistive technologies are enumerated. Downgraded from P0 to P1 and reclassified as partial coverage.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Five documents require that a map declare 'سیستم مختصات' (coordinate system): 09, 12, 14, 15, 17. Doc 25 includes projection in test items. No document defines EPSG identifiers, datum transformation, axis order, coordinate units or reprojection rules.
Technical or Documentation Impact: Geospatial output can be silently wrong because no approved CRS or transformation rule exists.
Notes: Prior report labelled this 'not covered'. Incorrect: the requirement to declare a CRS exists in five documents. The missing element is the CRS standard and the project CRS selection. P0 for map work, P1 for the sequence.

Actual Statement or Requirement: Doc 34 §15.3 defines a transaction lifecycle CREATED, PENDING, FAILED, EXPIRED, CONFIRMED and states the real states must come from the financial service contract. §15.4 forbids showing payment success before backend confirmation. §15.5 requires duplicate prevention. §15.6 defines unknown-state handling.
Technical or Documentation Impact: The requirement is documented; the concrete state set is explicitly deferred to the service contract.
Notes: Prior report claimed no transaction-state standard exists. Incorrect. Reclassified as a contract decision inside A34, not a documentation gap.
